Class Slots

java.lang.Object
com.trevorschoeny.menukit.inject.Slots
@Internal public final class Slots extends Object
The one place a slot in a screen's menu.slots is resolved to the real vanilla Slot it represents — itself on most screens, or the slot a creative SlotWrapper delegates to on the creative inventory tab.

Why this is the foundation, not a slot detail

The creative inventory tab wraps every player-inventory slot in a SlotWrapper whose getContainerSlot() reports the wrapper's own index. So any code reading a slot's identity off menu.slots — "which player-inventory slot is this?" (a vanilla concern, e.g. anchoring a panel to the hotbar) or "is this one of my slots?" (a containers concern) — gets the wrong answer on creative unless it unwraps first. target(Slot) is that unwrap, shared by both:
  • VanillaSlotResolver reads target.container + target.getContainerSlot() to find a vanilla player-inventory slot's on-screen position;
  • MenuKit-Containers' MKCSlotAccess.asMKCSlot tests whether target is a registered slot.
Before this, only slots could see through the wrapper (asMKCSlot); a non-slot vanilla slot was unreachable on creative — the gap that left hotbar-anchored slots (pockets) dark there. One unwrap path closes it for everyone.

Client-only: the creative wrapper is a client type. Only client-side render + input + anchoring code calls this.

Internal plumbing. The creative-wrapper unwrap is a library-internal detail of how MK resolves a raw vanilla Slot's identity; it is not a consumer surface. Consumers address slots by Address, never by handing MK a raw Slot to unwrap.

    • target

      public static net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot target(net.minecraft.world.inventory.Slot slot)
      The real vanilla Slot slot is or wraps: the slot a creative SlotWrapper delegates to, or slot itself when it is not a wrapper. Single-level — creative wraps each slot exactly once.

      Read identity (container, container-index, registered type) off the returned target; read on-screen position (x/y) off the original slot, which is the wrapper carrying the creative coordinates.
